q: Name the sweet appellations of the right bank facing Sauternes across the Garonne (any two).
exp: Same mists, humbler prices — the somm's by-the-glass botrytis answer.

q: Characterize 1982 Bordeaux and its critical consequence.
accept: ripe opulent early drinking made parker's career
ans: Hot, ripe, opulent, precociously drinkable — the vintage Robert Parker championed against the British establishment, making both his name and the modern points economy
exp: Left Bank's benchmark of generosity; still magnificent.

q: Contrast 2009 and 2010 Bordeaux in one sentence each.
accept: 2009 opulent ripe lower acid 2010 structured higher acid tannin
ans: 2009: warm, hedonistic, plush, lower acid; 2010: equally ripe but higher acid and tannin — the classical, longer-haul twin
exp: The 'which do you cellar?' question answers itself: 2010.

q: Name three difficult modern Bordeaux vintages and their defining problem.
exp: Master orals ask for the mechanism, not just the verdict.

q: Name the seven varieties approved in 2021 for climate adaptation in Bordeaux AOC.
accept: touriga nacional marselan castets arinarnoa alvarinho liliorila petit manseng
ans: Reds: Touriga Nacional, Marselan, Castets, Arinarnoa. Whites: Alvarinho, Liliorila, Petit Manseng
exp: Capped at 5% of plantings and 10% of the blend — a legal experiment.

q: Recite the six grands crus of Vosne-Romanée, in any order.
accept: romanee-conti la tache richebourg romanee-saint-vivant la romanee la grande rue
ans: Romanée-Conti, La Tâche, Richebourg, Romanée-Saint-Vivant, La Romanée, La Grande Rue
exp: Échezeaux and Grands Échezeaux belong to Flagey — the classic follow-up trap.

q: Which grand cru did La Grande Rue become in 1992, and whose monopole is it?
ans: Promoted to grand cru in 1992; monopole of Domaine François Lamarche
exp: It runs uphill between La Tâche and Romanée-Conti — promotion was overdue.

q: Name all nine grands crus of Gevrey-Chambertin.
accept: chambertin clos de beze chapelle charmes griotte latricieres mazis mazoyeres ruchottes
ans: Chambertin, Chambertin-Clos de Bèze, Chapelle-, Charmes-, Griotte-, Latricières-, Mazis-, Mazoyères-, Ruchottes-Chambertin
exp: Clos de Bèze may sell as plain Chambertin; Mazoyères as Charmes.

q: Explain the 1935 'Appellation d'Origine Contrôlée' inaugural link to Burgundy: which wine claims AOC no. 1 by decree date?
accept: first decrees 1936 arbois cassis chateauneuf tavel monbazillac
ans: The first 1936 decrees honored Arbois, Cassis, Châteauneuf-du-Pape, Monbazillac and Tavel — Burgundy followed within months
exp: A Master favorite: Châteauneuf's Baron Le Roy wrote the template, the first wave was multi-regional.

q: What are the two lieux-dits that compose Corton-Charlemagne's historic core, and the emperor's connection?
ans: En Charlemagne and Le Charlemagne — vines Charlemagne granted to Saulieu's abbey in 775
exp: The white-wine legend of the queen and the beard attaches here.

q: Describe 'provignage' and name the Champagne/Burgundy relic vineyards that still use it.
accept: layering vines burying cane to root new vine
bollinger vieilles vignes francaises romanee-conti pre-1945
ans: Layering: burying a cane to root a new vine — pre-phylloxera propagation (Bollinger's VVF; DRC's Romanée-Conti until 1945)
exp: Romanée-Conti's last ungrafted harvest was 1945; replanted 1947.

q: Which abbey planted Clos de Bèze and when, and under what shorter grand cru name may its wine legally be sold?
ans: The Abbey of Bèze planted it c. 630 — the oldest documented Burgundy cru; under the 1936 decree it may be labelled simply 'Chambertin', though Chambertin may never be sold as Clos de Bèze
exp: Bertin's field ('champ Bertin') next door borrowed the fame.

q: Give the appellation and producer of 'Musigny Blanc' and its current legal curiosity.
ans: Comte Georges de Vogüé — the only white Musigny; declassified to Bourgogne Blanc since 1994 while young vines mature (returning as Musigny)
exp: A grand cru estate voluntarily labeling regional — Masters love the paradox.

q: Name the climat and commune of Domaine Leflaive's leading premier cru white, the one adjoining Bienvenues-Bâtard-Montrachet.
exp: Anne-Claude Leflaive's biodynamic conversion made it a movement flagship.

q: Explain 'rebêche' — trick question: where does the term actually belong?
accept: champagne pressing final cut not burgundy
ans: Champagne, not Burgundy — the final press fraction after the cuvée and taille, sent to distillation
exp: Masters exams cross-wire regions to test composure.

q: Which Mâconnais village AOP was promoted with premiers crus in 2020 — the first in the Mâcon?
exp: Rully etc. had them in the Chalonnaise; the Mâcon waited a century.
